evidence: The electronic properties of the Al doped MoS2 films, their composition, and their crystallinity were studied for various doping cycle ratios. Special attention was paid to the doping profile of the Al in the Al:MoS2 films which was studied by cross-section transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping. The chemical composition of the Al:MoS2 films was determined by XPS surface scans. The Raman response of the doped MoS2 films showed only minimal changes compared to the intrinsic film. The resistivity was calculated from the sheet resistance using film thickness determined by spectroscopic ellipsometry. The Hall voltage generated in the intrinsic sample was below the detection limit of the measurement system, the carrier density was estimated from the resistivity assuming a mobility similar to that of the lowest doped film. The impact of the doping on macroscopic aspects such as the chemical composition, crystal structure, and the crystallinity of the doped films will also be investigated. The XPS depth profile by Ar sputtering was also performed on the same sample. The resistivity was calculated from the sheet resistance using film thickness determined by spectroscopic ellipsometry. The Raman response of the doped MoS2 films showed only minimal changes compared to the intrinsic film. The XPS measurements also gave qualitative insight into the trend of the Al doping concentration with doping cycle ratio. The XPS results indicate that Al is not bound to Mo or Al, ruling out (i) the formation of large metallic clusters and (ii) Al occupying a S site. The position of the Al2p peak suggests that the Al is bonded to S. The XPS depth profile by Ar sputtering was also performed on the same sample.
